title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles
wiki_lead:
Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (TMNT) is an American media franchise created by comic book artists Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird. It follows Leonardo, Donatello, Raphael and Michelangelo, four anthropomorphic turtle brothers trained in ninjutsu who fight evil in New York City. The franchise encompasses printed media, television series, feature films, video games, and merchandise.
The franchise began as a comic book, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, which Eastman and Laird conceived as a parody of elements popular in superhero comics at the time. The first issue was published in 1984 by Eastman and Laird's company Mirage Studios and was a surprise success. In 1987, Eastman and Laird licensed the characters to Playmates Toys, which developed a line of Turtles action figures. About $1.1 billion worth of Turtles toys were sold between 1988 and 1992, making them the third-bestselling toy figures ever at the time.
The action figures were promoted with an animated series, which premiered in 1987 and ran for almost a decade. It was succeeded by several other television series. The first Turtles video game was released in 1989, the first of several developed by the Japanese company Konami. The first Turtles film, released in 1990, became the highest-grossing independent film up to that point.
Eastman sold his share of the Turtles franchise to Laird in 2000. In 2009, Laird sold it to Viacom, now Skydance. The franchise has continued with a new comic book series, television series, films and video games.

History


1983–1986: conception and first comics

The comic book authors Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird met in Massachusetts and began working on illustrations together. In 1983, Laird invited Eastman to move in with him in Dover, New Hampshire. That November, Eastman drew a masked turtle standing on its hind legs armed with nunchucks to make Laird laugh. Laird added the words "teenage mutant". The concept parodied several elements popular in superhero comics of the time — the teenagers of New Teen Titans, the mutants of Uncanny X-Men and the ninja skills of Daredevil — combined with the comic tradition of funny animals such as Howard the Duck.

Eastman and Laird developed the concept into a comic book. They considered giving the turtles Japanese names, but instead named them after the Italian Renaissance artists Leonardo, Donatello, Raphael, and Michelangelo, which Laird said "felt just quirky enough to fit the concept". They developed a backstory referencing further elements of Daredevil: like Daredevil, the Turtles are altered by radioactive material, and their sensei, Splinter, is a play on Daredevil's sensei, Stick.
In March 1984, Eastman and Laird founded a comic book company, Mirage Studios, in their home. Using money from a tax refund and a loan from Eastman's uncle, they printed copies of the first issue of Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles and advertised it in Comics Buyer's Guide. grok_lead: The Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles (TMNT) is an American multimedia franchise centered on four anthropomorphic teenage turtle brothersâLeonardo, Michelangelo, Donatello, and Raphael âwho are trained as ninjas by their rat sensei, Splinter, to battle evil in New York City, often while indulging in pizza and pop culture. Created by comic artists Kevin Eastman and Peter Laird as a satirical parody of popular 1980s comics like Daredevil and Ronin, the concept emerged from a late-night joke in November 1983 when Eastman sketched a masked turtle wielding nunchaku, prompting Laird to add the "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles" title in homage to existing trends. The first issue was independently published by their Mirage Studios imprint in May 1984, with an initial print run of 3,000 copies that sold out at a local comics convention, marking the start of an unexpected cultural phenomenon. The franchise quickly expanded beyond comics, launching a syndicated animated television series in 1987 that ran for 10 seasons and introduced catchphrases like "cowabunga" to a global audience, followed by three live-action films starting with Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles in 1990, which grossed over $200 million worldwide. Subsequent adaptations include a CGI-animated series from 2003 to 2009, a 2012 Nickelodeon reboot that aired until 2017, and more recent entries like the 2014 and 2016 live-action reboots produced by Paramount Pictures, alongside the critically acclaimed animated film Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem in 2023. Video games, such as the long-running TMNT arcade titles from Konami, and extensive toy lines from Playmates Toys have been staples, with the latter driving much of the franchise's commercial dominance. By the mid-1990s, TMNT had become one of the highest-grossing media properties of its era, amassing $6 billion in merchandise revenue alone up to that point, and the franchise has generated over $8 billion in global retail sales since 2012 through 2022, including over $1 billion in 2023 fueled by Mutant Mayhem 's success. The enduring appeal lies in its blend of action, humor, and themes of brotherhood and heroism, evolving across decades while maintaining core elements from the original Mirage comics, which continued until 2012 before licensing to IDW Publishing for ongoing series. As of 2025, the franchise continues to expand through IDW Publishing 's ongoing comic series and upcoming projects, including a sequel to Mutant Mayhem.
